examples.note: Rarotonga — the 2 prefix routes to the main island subscriber network

notes: The Cook Islands use a short 5-digit NSN with no trunk prefix or area codes.
Self-governing in free association with New Zealand, but with its own country code +682 rather than sharing +64.
sources: ITU-T E.164 national numbering plans: https://www.itu.int/oth/T0202.aspx

examples.note: Mobile — the 90 prepaid range, one digit longer than fixed

notes: Each of Tuvalu's nine atolls has its own dialling code (20–29), with Funafuti holding two (20 and 21).
Fixed NSNs are 5 digits and mobile NSNs 6.
sources: ITU-T E.164 national numbering plans: https://www.itu.int/oth/T0202.aspx

examples.note: Norfolk Island — area code 3 within +672, fixed range 2X

notes: Norfolk Island shares country code +672 with the Australian Antarctic Territory, taking area code 3.
Christmas Island and the Cocos (Keeling) Islands also used +672 until October 1994, when they migrated to +61.
+672 was assigned to Portuguese Timor until 1975, and +672 9 was used for Timor-Leste under an interim arrangement after 1999.
sources: ACMA — Australian Communications and Media Authority: https://www.acma.gov.au/numbering

notes: Niue has one of the shortest numbering plans in the world: most numbers are just 4 digits.
An updated ITU-registered plan took effect on 2018-05-01, adding a 7-digit LTE mobile range alongside the 4-digit numbers.
Telecom Niue is the sole provider.

examples.note: Tokelau — 5-digit number after the November 2015 expansion

notes: Tokelau moved from 4-digit to 5-digit numbers in November 2015 by prefixing '2' to existing numbers.
The registered plan permits 3 to 7 digits, but numbers in service are 5 digits.
Tokelau is a New Zealand territory but holds its own country code +690.
Wallis and Futuna is a French overseas collectivity but keeps its own country code +681 rather than joining the French plan.
All numbers are 6 digits with no trunk prefix; they are written in pairs in the French style.
sources: ITU-T E.164 national numbering plans: https://www.itu.int/oth/T0202.aspx

examples.note: Diego Garcia — the 37X fixed range (this specific number is a network test tone)

notes: The British Indian Ocean Territory's only inhabited island is Diego Garcia, a joint UK–US military facility; there is no civilian population.
Note the collision risk: +246 is the BIOT country code, while 246 is also the NANP area code for Barbados (+1 246). These are entirely different numbers.
No area codes; the NSN is a flat 7 digits.
sources: ITU — Diego Garcia (country code +246) numbering plan: https://www.itu.int/dms_pub/itu-t/oth/02/02/T02020000390001MSWE.doc

examples.note: Davis Station — Australian Antarctic Division numbering
Scott Base (NZ) and the nearby US McMurdo Station are reached through New Zealand's +64, not +672

notes: Antarctica has no public telephone network. Calls reach research stations over satellite links, and each national programme numbers its own bases.
+672 covers the Australian Antarctic Territory bases (Davis, Mawson, Casey) plus Macquarie Island — it is shared with Norfolk Island, which uses area code 3.
New Zealand's Scott Base and the US McMurdo Station are reached via +64; other national programmes use their own home country codes or Iridium/Inmarsat satellite numbers (+870 range).
ISO 3166-1 assigns AQ to Antarctica as a whole, but no single numbering plan covers the continent.
sources: Australian Antarctic Program — communicating with Antarctica: https://www.antarctica.gov.au/antarctic-operations/family-and-friends/introductory-package/communicating-with-antarctica-by-phone-and-email/

examples.note: Christmas Island — the dedicated 9164 exchange within Australia's 08 area code

notes: Christmas Island is an Australian external territory inside the +61 plan; it has no country code of its own.
It used +672 until October 1994, when it migrated to +61 and eventually settled on the 08 9164 range.
Administered by ACMA under the Australian Telecommunications Numbering Plan.
sources: ACMA — Australian Communications and Media Authority: https://www.acma.gov.au/numbering

examples.note: Cocos (Keeling) Islands — the dedicated 9162 exchange within Australia's 08 area code

notes: The Cocos (Keeling) Islands are an Australian external territory inside the +61 plan; they have no country code of their own.
They used +672 until October 1994, when they migrated to +61 and eventually settled on the 08 9162 range.
Christmas Island uses the adjacent 08 9164 range.
sources: ACMA — Australian Communications and Media Authority: https://www.acma.gov.au/numbering

notes: Pitcairn has no numbering plan of its own and no local exchange. With a population of a few dozen, the island is served by satellite.
Contact numbers for the Pitcairn Islands administration are New Zealand +64 numbers, and the island itself has historically been reached over Inmarsat satellite numbers in the +872 range.
ISO 3166-1 assigns PN, but no country calling code is allocated to the territory.
sources: Government of the Pitcairn Islands: https://www.government.pn/

notes: Bouvet Island is an uninhabited subantarctic dependency of Norway. It has no permanent population, no exchange and no telephone numbers.
It is nominally associated with Norway's +47 country code, but no numbers are allocated to it and none are reachable.
Any communication with expeditions on the island is by satellite.
Heard Island and McDonald Islands form an uninhabited Australian external territory in the subantarctic. There is no permanent population and no exchange.
The territory is nominally associated with +672, the Australian Antarctic code, but no numbers are allocated to it.
Australian Antarctic Division expeditions that visit communicate by satellite.
sources: Australian Antarctic Program — Heard Island: https://heardisland.antarctica.gov.au/

notes: The French Southern and Antarctic Lands have no permanent civilian population — only rotating scientific and military staff at bases on the Kerguelen and Crozet islands, Amsterdam Island and Adélie Land.
The territory is administered from Réunion and falls nominally under +262, but no public subscriber numbers are allocated.
Station communications run over satellite links operated by the French polar institute IPEV and the territorial administration.
sources: Terres australes et antarctiques françaises: https://taaf.fr/

formats.international: military circuits reached through US ranges

notes: The United States Minor Outlying Islands are a statistical grouping of nine uninhabited or minimally staffed islands (Baker, Howland, Jarvis, Johnston Atoll, Kingman Reef, Midway, Navassa, Palmyra, Wake). None has a civilian numbering plan.
Wake Island and Midway Atoll, the only ones with any regular staffing, are reached through US military circuits historically routed via the Hawaii area code +1 808.
There is no ISO-territory-specific country code or area code; ISO 3166-1 assigns UM for statistical purposes only.
